notes: Aeronautical data (ARP, elevation, MAG VAR, runways, thresholds, declared distances, obstacle heights) are from the UAE GCAA eAIP AD 2 pages, AIRAC AMDT 12/2026 package (published 15 OCT 2026, effective 26 NOV 2026). They were diffed against the AMDT 09/2026 package in force on 2026-10-26: AD 2.2/2.12/2.13 are identical except the OMDB MAG VAR entry and a new OMSJ runway-maintenance remark.
Coordinates are WGS-84. AIP DMS strings are kept in aip_dms; decimals converted exactly. Feet converted with 0.3048 m/ft.

true_bearings_deg are the AIP-published true bearings (integers for OMAA/OMDB, 2 decimals for OMSJ). true_bearings_deg_computed and length_m_computed_* are geodesic values (WGS-84, Vincenty inverse) computed by us from the AIP threshold/runway-end coordinates.
thresholds[].lat/lon are the landing thresholds (displaced where displaced_m > 0). For OMDB and OMSJ the physical pavement ends are in runway_ends.
Building dimensions marked approximate/OSM come from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors) and are cross-check values only; pipeline/osm is the authoritative footprint source.

Photos: only Wikimedia Commons files licensed CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC0 or public domain were kept. License, author and date were read from each file page via the Commons API (extmetadata) on 2026-10-26 and spot-checked on the HTML file pages. GFDL-only files (e.g. the Airliners.net "AN" series) and Free Art License files were excluded. No image files were downloaded. Attribution (author + license) is required for CC BY / CC BY-SA images; CC BY-SA requires share-alike for adaptations.
The diagrams lists (extra key) hold openly licensed layout diagrams, not photos.

Some pages could not be fetched (DAEP: Cloudflare check; Archnet: Vercel bot check; adairports.ae: 403; WAM/TradeArabia: unavailable). Facts attributed to those URLs come from search-engine result text and are flagged in the descriptions.
Conflicting values are listed side by side (alt_values / *_alt_values) with sources; the preferred value is the primary source (AIP, operator fact file, architect).

OMAA.name: Zayed International Airport
former_names: Abu Dhabi International Airport (renamed Zayed International Airport on 9 February 2024)

arp.site: Mid point of RWY 13R/31L, on CL

alt_values.note: Wikipedia infobox differs from AIP; use AIP

runways.notes: Southern runway (the original runway, airport opened 1982). No displaced thresholds (THR = runway end; LDA = TORA). ARP lies on its centreline at mid-length. CL separation from 13L/31R = 2000 m (AIP). Closed for preventive maintenance Tue/Thu/Sat 1130-1430 UTC (AIP). Wikipedia infobox gives 4,205 m for both runways - AIP value used.

Northern runway, opened October 2008 (Wikipedia). No displaced thresholds. Closed for preventive maintenance Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun 1130-1430 UTC (AIP). Terminal A and the ATC tower sit in the midfield between the two runways.

terminals.name: Terminal A (formerly Midfield Terminal Building / Midfield Terminal Complex)
terminals.opened: 2023-10-31 (official opening and first Etihad departure; all airlines operating from Terminal A from 2023-11-14)
area_alt_values: 7.9 million sq ft ~ 734,000 m2 (KPF news, construction-era)
terminals.gates_detail: 51 contact gates (14 MARS-capable), expandable to 65 contact gates in full MARS configuration, plus 6 remote bus gates; Terminal A apron (Apron 6) = 51 (65) contact + 14 remote stands; airport-wide 64 passenger + 30 cargo stands (ACL W26 capacity declaration, published 30/04/26). ADA/KPF: up to 79 aircraft at any one time; Hill International: piers accommodate up to 65 aircraft.
terminals.capacity_note: 45 mppa today, 11,000 pax/hour; KPF: designed for up to 80 mppa.
terminals.architect: Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates (KPF) - design competition won 2006

architecture.plan_shape: X-shaped: a central processor / departure hall with four piers radiating from a central hub; piers themed desert, sea, city and oasis. KPF refined the plan from linear, Y, H and modified-X schemes; the centre was shifted to align with the runway axis and the entrance rotated toward the arrival road from downtown. Sits midfield between the two runways, raised on its own plateau above road level.
architecture.roof: Single continuous undulating metal roof informed by sand dunes: the arch-shaped pier geometry is pulled down at each segment, giving a wave/dune profile; roof drapes over the facade (reduces glazing, no external shading devices). Central departure hall roof carried on 18 curved steel arches (visually separated from the roof), the largest about 180 m span and 52 m high; the central arch kept low enough for aircraft to fly over.

dimensions_m.osm_overall_extent_approx: ~1,400 m E-W x ~1,420 m N-S; minimum bounding rectangle ~1,190 x 1,080 m; footprint ~234,000 m2 (OSM relation 20328079, ODbL; approximate)

architecture.height_note: Ceiling at highest point 52 m (Hill International; arch height 52 m per AviationWeek 2016); departure hall 50 m (KPF); OSM height tag 53 m; AIP obstacle "MIDFIELD TERMINAL COMPLEX" top elevation 259 ft AMSL at 242707.6N 0543825.6E (~54 m above the 83 ft aerodrome elevation; derived, approximate).
architecture.facade: Glass and aluminium: ~115,000 m2 external glazing and ~275,000 m2 aluminium cladding (Hill International). Free-standing 50 m tall glazed landside facade; glazed pier facades canted outward at 14.75 deg to shade the holdrooms; glass with a fading frit pattern that becomes more transparent toward the top (KPF).
architecture.colours: Not documented in sources: metallic (aluminium) roof and large glazed facades - take colours from the reference photos.
architecture.features: Column-free central departure hall with mosaic stone flooring; two four-storey buildings flank the departure hall (hotel rooms and offices) (Dezeen); "Sana Al Nour" light/air feature 22 m tall x 30 m wide made of 1,632 curved glass leaves; "The Shell" brass and Cor-Ten sculpture wrapped in glass; skylights for wayfinding; 3,400 covered short-term + 1,500 long-term parking spaces; Estidama 3 Pearl; visible from the highway >1.5 km away.

terminals.name: Former Terminal 1
terminals.status: closed (all flights moved to Terminal A by 14 Nov 2023)
terminals.gates_detail: Nine jet-bridge gates (3-11) in a circular gate area plus bus gates 14-22 (Wikipedia).

architecture.plan_shape: Main building plus a circular satellite gate area (Wikipedia). OSM outline ~330 x 300 m, footprint ~37,000 m2 (approximate).
architecture.features: Old ATC tower nearby (AIP obstacle "OLD ATCC TOWER" 242533.7N 0543848.6E, top 231 ft AMSL).

architecture.plan_shape: Small single building; OSM footprint ~12,700 m2 (~135 x 116 m), approximate.

terminals.name: Former Terminal 3
terminals.gates_detail: 34 gates, 8 with jet bridges, 2 A380-capable (Wikipedia); interim AED 1 bn facility used mainly by Etihad.

architecture.plan_shape: Linear building; OSM minimum bounding rectangle ~730 x 220 m, footprint ~44,600 m2 (approximate).

control_towers.name: Air Traffic Control Complex (ATCC) tower
height_alt_values: AIP AD 2.10 obstacle "OMAA AD 001 / ATCC Tower": height 378 ft (115.2 m) above ground, top elevation 455 ft AMSL (likely includes masts/appurtenances)
110 m (2006 design announcement, TradeArabia; OSM tag height=110)
109 m, 20 storeys (Gulf News c.2010; Airport Technology)
control_towers.opened: 2011 (structure completed per Airport Technology / Terrell; earlier reports targeted 2008-2010)
control_towers.shape: Tall curved crescent / sail-like blade shaft with the visual control cab at the top, rising from a 5-storey rectangular technical base building
control_towers.description: Designed by ADPi (Aeroports de Paris Ingenierie; design and supervision contract July 2006). Braced, curved steel tower structure over a reinforced-concrete 5-storey base with one basement; ~7,000 m2 floor area; 20 storeys (Terrell; Airport Technology). Its "swaying curves" were described as resembling the crescent moon, a dhow sail or a broadsword blade (TradeArabia 2006, page no longer online - text known from search-engine snippet). Stands in the midfield exactly between the two runways (~1.0 km from each centreline, computed from AIP coordinates), ~1.8 km along from the 13R threshold.

control_towers.name: Old ATCC tower (near former Terminal 1)
control_towers.description: Listed in AIP AD 2.10 as obstacle "OMAA AD 019 / OLD ATCC TOWER", top elevation 231 ft AMSL (height not published, roughly 45-50 m above ground - derived, approximate). OSM "Old Control Tower" footprint ~35 x 35 m.

cargo.description: Etihad Cargo hub. Existing cargo area lies on the south side next to the former terminals; a new East Midfield Cargo Terminal is under construction. 2024 cargo throughput 678,990 t (ADA via Wikipedia).
facilities: Existing "Cargo Terminal" building near 24.4230 N, 54.6534 E: ~362 x 112 m, footprint ~39,500 m2 (OSM way 62271383, approximate)
"Abu Dhabi Cargo Village" warehouse ~9,100 m2 footprint (OSM way 167460164, approximate)

East Midfield Cargo Terminal (EMCT): ~90,000 m2, design capacity 1-1.5 million t/yr, ground broken December 2024 (RAQ Contracting), opening planned late 2027 (Stattimes / Construction Briefing; via search summaries)
ACL W26 declaration: 9 additional stands for cargo operations; cargo-ops stand summary Code F 3, Code E 27 (30 total)

OMDB.name: Dubai International Airport

arp.site: On CL RWY 12R/30L, at the displaced threshold of RWY 12R

magnetic_variation.note: AIRAC AMDT 12/2026 (effective 26 NOV 2026) changes this entry to 2 deg E (2026) / 0.00 deg; the edition in force on 2026-10-26 (AMDT 09/2026) reads 2 deg E (2020) / 0.05 deg E.

runways.strip: 280 m wide over full length, 60 m beyond each pavement end
runways.shoulders: 7.5 m load-bearing asphalt shoulders + 10 m non-load-bearing sealed area each side
runways.notes: Southern runway. Displaced thresholds: 12R by 715 m, 30L by 132 m. ARP is at the 12R displaced threshold. Resurfaced and relit during a 45-day closure 16 Apr - 30 May 2019. Designators unchanged: no renumbering found (current AIP, Wikipedia, ACL and AIN 2022 all use 12R/30L and 12L/30R). 180-degree turns not permitted for aircraft larger than A320.

runways.strip: 280 m wide over full length, 60 m beyond each pavement end
runways.shoulders: 7.5 m load-bearing asphalt shoulders + 12.5 m non-load-bearing sealed area each side
runways.notes: Northern runway. Displaced thresholds: 12L by 450 m, 30R by 300 m. Centreline separation ~384 m (computed from AIP coordinates; Wikipedia 385 m). Wikipedia body text still says 4,000 x 60 m (AIN 2022: 13,120 ft) - the AIP pavement length is 4,351 m (LDA 3,600/4,000 m). Closed 9 May - 22 June 2022 for the Northern Runway Rehabilitation (resurfacing, strip strengthening, AGL replacement). Designators unchanged (no renumbering found).

stands_summary.note: ACL S26 slot-coordination declaration (delivered 01/10/2025, "PUBLIC - OPEN DATA"). Declared stands can be fewer than physical gates (e.g. Concourse A has 20 A380 contact gates).

terminals.name: Terminal 1
terminals.opened: 1971 (original building, 15 May 1971); refurbished 2013-2015 and again later
area_alt_values: 520,000 m2 (Wikipedia, probably includes Concourses C/D - not used)
terminals.gates_detail: Gates are in Concourse D (and formerly Concourse C); T1 has check-in rows 1-5 + Area 6 (42 counters each in rows 1-4).
terminals.capacity_note: "more than 20 million" (Dubai Airports T1 fact file); Wikipedia says 45 mppa.

architecture.plan_shape: Rectangular landside processor, 502 x 125 m, 3 floors (excluding roof); connected airside to Concourse D by an elevated people mover and historically to Concourse C (Sheikh Rashid Terminal).

dimensions_m.osm_min_rect_approx: 651 x 127 m, footprint ~65,200 m2 (OSM way 98425196; outline likely includes link structures)

architecture.features: The original 1971 building featured ogee arches that are still present (Wikipedia). Apron floor area 54,458 m2, departure floor 40,207 m2 (fact file).

terminals.name: Concourse D (serves Terminal 1)
terminals.gates_detail: 32 gates incl. 4 Code F: 21 contact + 11 remote (fact file); second fact-file table lists Code E 12, Code C 1, Code F 4 gates with lounges and 11 remote stands; ACL S26 declares 18 contact stands (6 C, 11 E, 1 F).
terminals.capacity_note: 18 mppa (2023 fact file); 15 mppa at opening (Wikipedia).

architecture.plan_shape: Linear pier/concourse built around a central atrium, open-gate concept; linked to T1 by a 2-minute elevated rail people mover (5 cars, 300 pax).
architecture.features: 4 floors incl. service floor; 450 m2 of solar panels; cost AED 3.35 bn incl. APM.

terminals.name: Concourse C (Sheikh Rashid Terminal; part of Terminal 3 complex since 2016)
terminals.gates_detail: 27 gates; 22 contact stands with passenger loading bridges; 21 remote stands (fact file). ACL S26 declares 20 contact stands (8 Code E, 12 Code F). Wikipedia: 50 gates incl. 28 air bridges (older).

architecture.plan_shape: Long straight concourse ~800 m (780.8 x 66.8 m), joined to Concourse B at the control-tower structure; 6 floors incl. basement.
architecture.features: Contains a hotel; departure floor 47,447 m2, apron floor 46,785 m2 (fact file).

terminals.name: Terminal 2
terminals.area_note: Departures 10,000 m2 + boarding 2,500 m2 built-up (fact file); Wikipedia 47,000 m2 (probably whole complex) - treat as approximate.
terminals.gates_detail: 12 bus gates (F1-F12), 43 remote stands, no jet bridges (fact file; Wikipedia).
terminals.capacity_note: "over 12 million" pax/yr (fact file); 2,200 arr + 1,700 dep pax/hour.

architecture.plan_shape: Low single-storey terminal on the north side of the airfield (fact file: north of Terminal 1, access from Al Twar Road and Rashidiya; ACL lists its aprons Echo/Quebec as North side), with the remote stands behind it.

dimensions_m.osm_min_rect_approx: 708 x 97 m, footprint ~59,100 m2 (OSM way 98425234; outline probably includes the boarding/remote-gate wing)

architecture.features: Home of flydubai since 1 June 2009. Executive Flight Terminal (business aviation) sits close by.

terminals.name: Terminal 3 (landside building)
area_alt_values: 1,713,000 m2 (Wikipedia - whole T3 complex incl. concourses)
terminals.gates_detail: Gates are in Concourses A, B and C.
terminals.capacity_note: T3 together with Concourse B added 43 mppa in 2008 (airport total to 60 mppa); Concourse A later added 15 mppa (to 75).
terminals.architect: Aeroports de Paris Ingenierie (ADPi) per Wikipedia (Dubai International Terminal 3); contractors Al Habtoor, Murray & Roberts, Takenaka

architecture.plan_shape: Landside processor largely BELOW the apron: departure and arrival halls ~10 m beneath apron level, directly connected underground to Concourse B; 6 floors.
architecture.features: 33,000 t structural steel; 3-floor 177,500 m2 car park with 1,889 spaces; Dubai Metro station (Sept 2009). US$4.5 bn incl. Concourse B. OSM maps only a ~299 x 25 m above-ground strip as "Terminal 3" (way 98425182) - most of the building is below apron level.

terminals.name: Concourse B (Terminal 3)
terminals.gates_detail: 25 contact stands + 6 remote gates (incl. 5 A380 gates), 59 passenger loading bridges (fact file); ACL S26 declares 20 contact stands (11 E, 9 F); Wikipedia: gates B1-B32, 26 with air bridges.

architecture.plan_shape: Very long, straight, symmetric airside concourse lying parallel to the runways, widest at the middle and tapering to both ends; joined to Concourse C at the control-tower structure and to T3 underground.
architecture.roof: Vaulted structural-steel roof along the concourse (BG&E: design of the "structural steel vaulted roof of the main concourse"); ~70,000 m2 standing-seam metal roofing (Al Abbar, via search summary).
architecture.facade: Glazed long facades under the vaulted metal roof (glazing and other cladding supplied by Al Abbar, via search summary); check photos for mullion pattern.
architecture.colours: Not documented: light metallic roof and glass - see photos.
architecture.features: 10 floors (4 basement + ground + 5). Hotel and lounges on upper levels; four SkyTrain elevators. Wikipedia instead gives 945 x 90.8 x 49.5 m - the official fact file values are used.

terminals.name: Concourse A (Terminal 3)
terminals.gates_detail: 20 contact gates all A380-capable + 2 Code E gates, plus 7 remote gates/lounges (13 remote stands in 2012 sheet) (fact files); ACL S26 declares 17 Code F contact stands.
terminals.architect: Not confirmed (T3 complex credited to ADPi on Wikipedia)

architecture.plan_shape: Free-standing midfield satellite east of Concourse B, linked by an underground automated people mover and service tunnels; "similar to Concourse B in appearance but with a smaller footprint".
architecture.roof: Long vaulted/arched metal roof in the same style as Concourse B (official fact file: similar appearance).

dimensions_m.osm_min_rect_approx: 655 x 104 m, footprint ~65,300 m2 (OSM way 231888210) - confirms ~645 m, not 924 m

architecture.facade: Glazed long facades under the arched roof (as Concourse B).
architecture.features: World's first purpose-built A380 concourse with multi-level boarding direct from First/Business lounges; central atrium with large "SkyTrain" elevators; 4- and 5-star hotels; 11 floors (2012 sheet) / 16 floors (later fact file). Wikipedia gives 924 x 91 x 40 m, which matches Concourse B and looks transposed - the official 645 x 90.8 x 42 m is used.

control_towers.name: DXB air traffic control tower (Dubai Air Navigation Services)
height_alt_values: AIP AD 2.10 obstacle "OMDB AD 18962 / ATC_AERIAL" (type CONTROL_TOWER): height 281 ft (85.6 m), top elevation 289 ft AMSL
control_towers.opened: 2000 (in operation since the 2000 expansion that opened Sheikh Rashid Terminal / Concourse C)
control_towers.shape: Buttressed central column with arched "wings", likened to a futuristic bird sculpture, topped by a multilevel control cab
control_towers.description: Stands at the junction of Concourses B and C (Wikipedia: the walkway link between Concourse B and Sheikh Rashid Terminal/Concourse C is "at the control tower structure"), ~560 m south-west of the 12R/30L centreline near the western end of the runway (computed from AIP coordinates); OSM maps a ~120 x 95 m terminal block around this junction (way 264966382). In June 2026 Dubai Airports unveiled a new tower design carrying the UAE flag (colours red, green, white, black); the exact paint pattern is not described in the sources - check current photos before texturing.

cargo.description: Dubai Airports cargo facilities (operated mainly by dnata) in the cargo village area; total DXB cargo capacity 3.3 million t/yr; 2024 throughput 2.2 million t. Freighter operations partly moved to DWC.
facilities: Cargo Mega Terminal (CMT): opened 2008, US$200 m, +1.2 million t (to 2.5 million t total); 57 docks (21 general, 10 truck, 12 perishables, 14 pharma)
Dubai Flower Centre: first phase 2004 (US$50 m), ~100,000 m2 planned, kept at 2-4 C; Freight Gates FG2-FG5 + DFC combined 720,000 t/yr
Air Cargo Terminal (ACT): 56 truck docks + 7 sea-air docks; Agents Building with 65 freight forwarders
FedEx (14,000 t) and DHL (75,000 t) facilities on the north side

OMSJ.name: Sharjah International Airport

arp.site: Mid-point of TWY B (about 255 m from the current runway centreline - computed)

alt_values.note: Wikipedia cites a 2013 AIP; current AIP says 119 ft

runways.notes: ONLY ONE runway is published. This is the "new runway" inaugurated 22 Oct 2014 (4,060 x 60 m, AED 500 m, design/supervision Halcrow, contractor Lane-NCTC, 8 new link taxiways + 2 rapid exits, CAT II). It was planned parallel to the original runway at ~250 m spacing (Airport Technology 2012). The AIP ARP ("mid-point of TWY B") lies ~255 m from the current centreline, consistent with the original runway now serving as parallel TWY B (inference, not stated by a source; TWY B published width 25 m). Both thresholds displaced by 300 m. A further additional runway was among plans reviewed in Feb 2025 (WAM) - not built/published. New in AIRAC AMDT 12/2026 (eff. 26 Nov 2026): runway closed for preventive maintenance every Tuesday 0600-0700 UTC.

OMSJ.aprons: AIP AD 2.8: MAIN APRON stands 1A-1C and 2-8 (stands 3-8 have fixed ground power); EASTERN APRON 9-26; WESTERN APRON 29-40; CARGO APRON 50-62; MAINTENANCE APRON 80-84; maintenance area F1-F2; VIP apron.

terminals.name: Passenger terminal
terminals.opened: 1977 (Sharjah Airport milestones; 1 January 1977 per Wikipedia; Gulf News 2008 says built 1978). Terminal expanded 2008 (milestones; Airport Technology describes a Dh227 m 2005-2009 expansion); new expansion under way, target 2027
terminals.gates_detail: 8 departure gates and 25 aircraft stands (Airport Technology, 2012); three air bridges added in the 2005-2009 expansion; AIP lists stands 1A-40 on the passenger aprons.
terminals.capacity_note: >8 mppa (2012). Expansion: 190,000 m2 terminal expansion (AED 1.235 bn) raising capacity to 20 mppa by 2027 (Gulf Construction Online, Feb 2024); SAA chairman: up to 25 mppa by mid-2027 (ME Construction News, Jun 2024).
terminals.architect: Not identified. Gulf News (2008) credits the design of the domes to H.H. Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Mohammad Al Qasimi, Ruler of Sharjah.

architecture.plan_shape: Compact terminal on the SOUTH side of the runway (~0.9 km from the runway centreline; parallel TWY B lies in between), composed around domes, with the original control tower standing beside it like a minaret.
architecture.roof: Domes of different sizes - four per Archnet (housing the main concourse, arrivals, departures and VIP areas), three per Gulf News 2008 - built as steel lattice structures clad in glass-reinforced plastic (GRP).

dimensions_m.osm_min_rect_approx: main terminal outline (OSM way 182512055 "Terminal 1") ~376 x 164 m, footprint ~33,300 m2, plus four small adjoining terminal buildings of 1,000-3,600 m2 each (approximate)

architecture.facade: Reinforced-concrete structure with pointed arches; the concrete arches are infilled with blue glazed-ceramic sun screens (Archnet).
architecture.colours: Light/white building with blue glazed-ceramic screens in the arches (Archnet); dome colour not documented - check photos.
architecture.features: Islamic-style architecture ("striking architectural features" - airport milestones page). The aerial photo below shows the "unique passenger terminal design".

control_towers.name: Original control tower (part of the 1977 terminal composition)
control_towers.description: Archnet: the control tower is "treated as a minaret" completing the composition with the domes. Height not published; the AIP AD 2.10 obstacle list does not include it.

control_towers.name: New ATC tower (2014 runway project)
control_towers.description: Sharjah Airport: "A new Air Tower Control was established ... for emergency situations" together with the October 2014 runway. Location/height not published in the sources found.

cargo.description: Sharjah Airport cargo centre (Freight Centre established 1979, expanded 1999 - airport milestones; first delegated cargo complex in the UAE per Gulf News): five cargo terminals beside a dedicated cargo apron; Sharjah Airport International Free Zone (SAIF Zone, operational since 1995) adjoins the airport.
facilities: Five cargo terminals, total floor area 32,000 m2: T1 charter operations, T2 imports/RA3 exports, T3 freight forwarders, T4 customs and overflow imports, T5 scheduled operations (export, CEIV pharma)
Dedicated cargo apron for up to 13 wide-body aircraft including 4 Code E stands (official); AIP CARGO APRON stands 50-62
Forwarder warehouses of 1,200 m2 each plus 10 warehouses of 200 m2; cold storage, animal pens
Capacity 500,000 t/yr; 332,796 t handled to Oct 2012 (Airport Technology, 2012)
